rules.description: Rule id (`no-empty-catch`, or `plugin/rule`) to a level or a level with options.

ambiguous-booleans.description: A plain `yes`, `no`, `on` or `off`: a boolean to YAML 1.1 parsers and a string to YAML 1.2 parsers.

async-suffix.description: An async method returning Task or ValueTask has a name that does not end in `Async`. Overrides, explicit interface implementations and `Main` are left alone (their names are not the method's to choose). Renaming needs the binding layer, so there is no fix.

document-start.description: The first document does not start with `---`.

file-scoped-namespace.description: A file whose only top-level member is a block-scoped namespace can use `namespace X;` and save a level of indentation. The fix needs C# 10, so it is unsafe; the formatter re-indents the body afterwards.

max-line-length.description: A line is longer than the configured number of characters.

no-duplicate-keys.description: An object has the same key twice; parsers disagree on which value wins.

no-empty-catch.description: A catch block with no statements and no comment swallows the exception silently.

possible-null-dereference.description: A member or element access on an expression the compiler's nullable analysis says may be null. Only code under `#nullable enable` is checked. Off by default: the compiler reports the same thing as CS8602.

prefer-null-coalescing.description: `a != null ? a : b` (or `a == null ? b : a`) for a name or member access `a` is `a ?? b`. The fix is unsafe because the type of the expression can change when `a` is a nullable value type.

remove-unused-usings.description: A `using` directive that nothing in the file needs (the compiler's hidden CS8019). Not reported in a file that has compiler errors or `#if` regions, because unresolved or inactive code could be the one using it.

sorted-keys.description: The keys of an object are not in alphabetical order.

order.description: Keys that come first, in this order; the rest follow alphabetically.

unreachable-code.description: A statement that can never run. At `fast` depth this is the statement after a `return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue` or `goto`; with the flow layer it also covers constant conditions and calls that do not return (`does_not_return` in `semantics:`). Only the first statement of a run is reported. Removing it is offered as an editor quick fix only, because unreachable code usually signals a bug.

non_returning_calls.description: Treat the code after a call that never returns (`[DoesNotReturn]`,                       `does_not_return` in `semantics:`) as unreachable. The compiler does not,                       so turn this off to report exactly what it reports (CS0162).

unused-assignment.description: A value is stored in a local variable and no path reads it before it is overwritten or the variable goes out of scope (a dead store). Variables that are captured or whose address is taken are not checked; a variable that is never read at all is reported by `unused-variable` instead.

unused-private-member.description: A private field, method, property or event that no file of the project uses (`analysis: deep`). Members with attributes, overrides, interface implementations, `extern` and `partial` methods are left alone.

unused-variable.description: A local variable or catch variable that is never used (the compiler's CS0168), or is only assigned constants and never read (CS0219). Variables captured by lambdas or local functions count as used.

using-order.description: Plain `using` directives of a file or namespace are not in alphabetical order (ordinal). Aliases, `using static` and `global using` stay where they are, and so does a list that has preprocessor directives in it. Comments on lines of their own stay where they are; a comment after a directive moves with it.

system_first.description: Put `System` and `System.*` before the other namespaces.

description: Configuration of Sudsy, the formatter and linter for C#, JSON and YAML.

analysis.description: Analysis depth for rules: fast (syntax only), standard (within each file), deep (adds project scope).

accessor_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the accessors of a property that is laid out on several lines: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them.

assignment_layout.description: Where the value after `=` or the body after `=>` goes when the line is too long: `compact` moves a binary expression, a conditional or a query to the next line and leaves any other value on the line; `fluid` also moves strings, collection expressions and property initializers, and any other value whose first line does not fit after the operator.

base_list_layout.description: The base list of a type (`: A, B`): `inline` keeps it on the line of the type name; `hanging` keeps it there when it fits and otherwise starts a line, with one base type per line.

blank_lines_between_members.description: Blank lines between the members of a type, namespace or enum: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one) and never adds one; `separate` also requires one between two members when either has a body, an attribute or a comment above it.

brace_newline.description: Opening braces of types, members, blocks and lambdas: `all` puts each on its own line (Allman); `none` keeps it on the line of the declaration or statement.

clause_keyword_line.description: `else`, `catch` and `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} else {`) unless a comment sits between them.

constructor_initializer_line.description: The `: base(...)` or `: this(...)` initializer of a constructor: `same_line` keeps it after the parameter list; `new_line` puts it on its own indented line.

do_while_line.description: The `while` of a `do` statement: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} while (x);`).

empty_braces.description: Braces with nothing between them: `space` prints `{ }`, `tight` prints `{}`.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

indent_nested_binary.description: Indent the operands of a binary expression that is itself an operand of a binary expression with an operator of another precedence (`a && b || c`).

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

indent_switch_section_block.description: Indent a block that is the only statement of a `case` section below its label; when false the block starts at the label's indentation.

initializer_collapse.description: Initializers and collection expressions: `preserve` keeps one expanded when the source has a line break in it; `always` puts one on a single line whenever it fits.

inline_accessor_bodies.description: Keep the body of an accessor on its line (`get { return x; }`) when it is one simple statement without comments and fits; otherwise the braces go on their own lines.

lambda_argument_hug.description: A lambda argument whose body can hang from the call's line: `last` hugs a block lambda that is the last argument; `sole` hugs a lambda (block or expression) only when it is the only argument.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

member_chain_break_on_block.description: Break a member chain one call per line when a call other than the last has an argument with a block body (a lambda), even if the chain would fit.

member_chain_keep_accesses.description: In a broken member chain a property access stays on the line of the call after it (`.A.B()` is one group) instead of starting a line of its own.

member_chain_min_calls.description: A chain of member accesses and calls with at least this many calls is broken one call per line when it does not fit on a line.

preprocessor_symbols.description: Conditional compilation symbols (`DEBUG`, `NET8_0`) defined when parsing, which decide the active branch of `#if`. Only the active branch is formatted.

switch_arm_layout.description: Layout of a switch expression arm: `inline` keeps `pattern => value` as one run of tokens; `assignment` lays out the value like the right-hand side of `=` (see `assignment_layout`).

trailing_commas.description: Trailing comma after the last element of initializers, collection expressions, enums and switch expressions: `preserve` keeps what the source has; `never` removes it; `multiline` adds one when the list is on several lines and removes it otherwise.

unbreakable_single_item_lists.description: Never break a list that holds one simple item: an attribute list with one attribute, a type argument list with one name, an index that is one name or literal.

wrapped_brace_line.description: Opening brace of an initializer or property pattern that is laid out on several lines: `creation` puts it on its own line for `new T { ... }` only; `all` also for an initializer nested in an assignment (`Prop = { ... }`) and for property patterns; `none` keeps it on the line of the expression.

semantics.description: Facts about methods that the flow analyses use.

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

exclude.description: Globs of files to leave alone, in addition to ignore files.

extends.description: Presets (`preset:<language>/<name>`) or config files, applied in order.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

include.description: Globs of the files to format and lint (everything when empty).

collapse.description: Objects and arrays on one line: `preserve` keeps one that has a line break between its brackets expanded and puts the others on one line if they fit; `always` puts every one that fits on one line; `never` puts every non-empty one on several lines; `opening_break` keeps an object expanded when a line break follows its opening brace and puts every array that fits on one line.

dialect.description: JSON or JSONC (comments, trailing commas); `auto` decides by file name.
